# `from dotenv` for [formats](/commands/categories/formats.md)

<div class='command-title'>Parse text as a .env file and create a record.</div>

## Command Type

`built-in`

## Signature

```> from dotenv {flags} ```


## Input/output types:

| input  | output |
| ------ | ------ |
| string | record |
## Examples

Read a .env file into a record.
```nu
> "PORT=8080
export NAME='my app'
# a comment
GREETING=\"hello ${NAME}\"" | from dotenv
╭──────────┬──────────────╮
│ PORT     │ 8080         │
│ NAME     │ my app       │
│ GREETING │ hello my app │
╰──────────┴──────────────╯
```

Use a default for a variable that isn't set.
```nu
> "URL=http://${APP_HOST:-localhost}:8080" | from dotenv
╭─────┬───────────────────────╮
│ URL │ http://localhost:8080 │
╰─────┴───────────────────────╯
```

Read a .env file from disk.
```nu
> open .env

```

Load a .env file into the environment.
```nu
> open .env | load-env

```

## Notes
Each line is `KEY=value`, optionally starting with `export`. Values can be unquoted, single-quoted or double-quoted, and quoted values can span lines. In unquoted and double-quoted values, `${NAME}` and `$NAME` expand to an earlier key of the file, or else to the environment variable; names ignore case, as in `$env`, so `a=2` after `A=1` sets `A` again. A bare `$NAME` is letters, digits and `_`, so `$HOST.local` reads HOST, and a `$` before anything else, as in `$5` or `$(command)`, stays as written: commands aren't run. Single quotes or `\$` keep a `$`. As in sh, `${NAME:-word}` gives `word` when NAME is unset or empty and `${NAME-word}` only when it's unset, while `${NAME:+word}` gives `word` when NAME is set and not empty and `${NAME+word}` when it's set at all, so a key holding `-` can't be referenced: `${MY-VAR}` gives MY, or `VAR` when it's unset. A line starting with `#` is a comment, and so is a `#` after a blank in an unquoted value. `open` reads files named like `.env`, `.env.local` or `prod.env` with this command, and `load-env` loads the record into the environment.
